purpose: PCA probe: can linear subspace find compositional structure that global cosine misses?
notes: PCA SEPARATES at all layers. Structure is low-rank linear. But PCA separation does not predict behavioral fusion/fission. Key finding: PRESENCE (PCA decode) != ADDRESSABILITY (transplant control). Facts linearly decodable even when behaviorally inseparable. Confirms BP-1, strengthens BP-9. A>B asymmetry: A-sep ~13x B-sep at late layers.

purpose: Attention analysis: does cross-fact attention predict behavioral fusion?
notes: Fusion is NOT attention-mediated. Cross-fact attention is slightly LOWER at fused layers. Last token overwhelmingly attends to fact A (HESK) over fact B (VORN), explaining the A>B PCA asymmetry. The fusion mechanism must be in the MLP or residual stream, not attention.

purpose: Component-level transplant: is fusion in attention, MLP, or the whole state?
notes: NEITHER attention-only NOR MLP-only transplant can flip fact B. Full transplant shifts B by +4.1 logits but each component alone shifts by at most ~1.1. Fusion is a WHOLE-STATE property of the residual stream, not localizable to any single transformer component. Confirms BP-2 (distributed state). Caveat: full transplant flips B at ALL layers including SEPARATE because donor model answers B incorrectly in World 10.

purpose: Trajectory analysis: do world trajectories converge at fused layers?
notes: Worlds ALWAYS diverge (never converge). FUSED layers diverge slowly (-1.2), SEPARATE layers diverge fast (-5.7). Fusion = world-insensitive computation. Fission = world-sensitive computation. Static trajectory metrics are too coarse — the behavioral transplant amplifies tiny directional differences through remaining layers. Native math must model SENSITIVITY TO PERTURBATION across layers, not just state geometry.

purpose: Layer-dependent behavioral distance via logit lens — does the model have a resolution layer where it selects the queried fact and suppresses the irrelevant one?
notes: First clean replicating non-R^n finding. Logit lens (final norm+unembedding applied at each layer) + JSD measures query-selective resolution: at layer 25, model amplifies queried fact behavioral signature (JSD 0.72-0.80) while suppressing irrelevant fact (JSD 0.01-0.11). Cosine stays 0.91-0.99 throughout. Replicates across 3 entity pairs x 2 query targets x 2 templates = 6 configs. HESK/VORN peaks earlier (L21). T3 template peaks later (L26) with weaker amplitude. purpose: Test whether Qwen3-0.6B supports a product-of-registers overwrite algebra via purely behavioral (no hooks/vectors) token-level setter and query operations
notes: FAIL: product-of-registers algebra not supported. 16 types instead of 4 (presentation entanglement). Last-write-wins at 27% (model has primacy bias - first mention dominates over later contradictory setters). Disjoint commutation at 56%. The model cannot reliably overwrite facts via in-context appending. This tells us that the model is not a clean register machine at the behavioral level. The primacy bias is a structural property: early tokens establish a world model that later tokens cannot easily override. This connects to the logit-lens resolution finding (resolution layer at L21-25 establishes which fact the model will use). Genuine non-R^n data: no vectors touched.

purpose: Test whether attention routing explains logit-lens resolution layer. Measures attention from query position to queried vs irrelevant entity tokens across all layers, compares to JSD ratio.
notes: PASS (confound ruled out): attention ratio does NOT explain JSD ratio. Correlation range -0.10 to +0.25, all well below 0.7 kill threshold. Attention to queried entity is already HIGH from L3 onward (~0.5-0.8 across ALL layers, not selective). JSD ratio spikes at L21-25 WITHOUT corresponding attention spike. QueryB case especially clear: attention ratio near 0 everywhere (KROT is second in prompt) yet JSD ratio peaks 62.43x at L24-25. The resolution layer finding is NOT reducible to attention routing. Something in the MLP/combined transformation creates selective amplification independent of attention weights.

purpose: Decompose resolution into attention vs MLP: hook post-attention (before MLP) and post-MLP states, apply logit lens, compare JSD ratios.
notes: SURPRISING: Resolution is already present AFTER attention, BEFORE the MLP. The attention WEIGHTS are not selective (attention_control_v1 showed r~0), but the attention OUTPUT is — meaning the resolution is in the VALUE space, not the key/query routing. The MLP modulates rather than creates the resolution: sometimes sharpens (+8.61 for HESK/VORN) and sometimes blurs (-15.46 for PLIM/KROT). The resolution is an emergent property of value-vector composition at resolution layers.

purpose: Test whether resolution layer generalizes to 3-fact worlds (3 entities × 2 values each = 8 worlds). Does the model suppress BOTH irrelevant facts simultaneously?
notes: Resolution generalizes to 3-fact worlds. All configs with clean baselines show resolution at L25 with ratios 10-42x. BOTH irrelevant facts are suppressed simultaneously and equally (HESK/VORN/KROT: irrel1=0.0195, irrel2=0.0194). Resolution strength correlates with baseline accuracy (4/4 → 10-42x; 2/4 → 1.7x). The last entity (PLIM queryC) resolves just as cleanly (28.59x) as the first, so the mechanism is not simply primacy. This is a general mechanism, not pairwise competition.

purpose: Causal test: inject query-A hidden state into query-B forward pass at each layer. Tests whether resolution layer is causally active.
notes: UNINFORMATIVE: full-state injection at ANY layer carries donor information through all remaining layers, producing identical logits regardless of injection point. This tells us the fact-identity signal is present at ALL layers (not created at L25) — the resolution layer AMPLIFIES an already-present signal, it does not create it. A meaningful causal test needs partial-state injection (targeted subspace patching), which requires R^n tools. The correlational logit-lens evidence (5 experiments) is the stronger proof path for now.

purpose: Test whether continuations produce the same DISTRIBUTION (not just greedy answer) across same-place histories. Strengthens continuation_congruence_v1 from argmax equality to full next-token distribution equality via sqrt(JSD).
notes: 100% DEFECT RATE at distributional level despite 97% greedy congruence. Same-place histories (identical greedy answers) produce SUBSTANTIALLY DIFFERENT full next-token distributions (JSD 0.07-0.45). Greedy congruence was lucky argmax agreement, not distributional identity. Repeat-ZOG continuations show lowest divergence (avg 0.168), corrections highest (0.275). The behavioral place defined by greedy answers is COARSER than the model's actual internal state. The native mathematics needs finer-grained equivalence classes.

purpose: Measure how output distribution entropy evolves across layers via logit lens. Connect resolution layer to distributional congruence failure.
notes: COMMITMENT BOTTLENECK: entropy drops to near-zero at L24-25 (0.05-0.30 bits, top-1 mass 0.99+) then JUMPS BACK UP to 5.5-7.7 bits in the final output. The model commits at L25 (near-certain of the answer) then re-broadens the distribution in the final layers. The argmax survives re-broadening but the distributional tails change. This explains the distributional congruence failure: the commitment bottleneck makes greedy answers congruent across histories, but the re-broadening re-injects history-dependent distributional structure.

purpose: Test whether the re-broadened final distribution carries meaningful history information or generic noise. Also investigate L27 vs final-output entropy discrepancy.

metrics.detail: Top divergent tokens between same-place histories are overwhelmingly history-related (entity values, variant capitalization). 5-7 of top 10 divergent tokens are fact-world values.

notes: Two findings: (1) The re-broadened distribution is MEANINGFUL, not noise. The model leaks information about the ENTIRE fact-world into every output position's distribution, not just the queried fact. Divergent tokens between same-place histories are dominated by entity values (big/small/hot/cold/red/blue) and their capitalizations. (2) Repetition narrows the distribution: dup variants have 2-3x lower entropy than std/rev. Connects to primacy bias. purpose: 4 code structures (nested_func, for_loop, class_method, try_except), 576 readouts
notes: class_method=zero amplification (attributes vs local vars). Cross-structure transfer 60-80% at tau=0.05.

purpose: Non-Qwen replication: Pythia-1.4B, StableLM-1.6B, Gemma-3-1b (432 readouts)
notes: Pythia=zero (insufficient code training). StableLM=intermediate (neutral>identity). Gemma=intermediate (pass>neutral>identity). Three architectures, three different amplification orderings. Universal: code continuations amplify.

purpose: Variable name length sensitivity: do long variable names (counter, total, result) show different omega patterns than short names (x, y)?

metrics.finding: Pattern invariant to name length; magnitude 2-3x higher for long names (result identity=0.132 vs x=0.050); same ranking: identity>type_check>heavy>neutral

notes: Omega is qualitatively variable-name-independent. Longer names produce higher amplification magnitude, consistent with richer token representation.

purpose: Multi-variable scope: does omega effect persist with 2+ variables in scope? Does inter-variable dependency modulate it?

metrics.finding: type_check 2.3x stronger in dual-var scope (0.165 vs 0.072 single-var); identity still amplifies; dual_interleaved slightly lower than dual_independent (0.056 vs 0.082 identity)

notes: Multi-variable scope strengthens type_check dramatically. Model finds type(x) more informative when more variables are in play. Variable interaction partially modulates omega but does not eliminate it.

purpose: Held-out prediction test: can omega trained on standard continuations predict novel perturbation types?
notes: Decisive held-out test. At tau=0.05, omega predictor beats naive baselines by +33pp. At tight tau, everything amplifies so baselines match. Category transfer works: code-like vs destructive ranking transfers perfectly.

purpose: Bootstrap CIs and permutation tests on core omega claims
notes: Analysis-only (no model runs). Cohen d=3.49 is enormous. All CIs exclude zero for amplifying continuations. N=7 eligible cells per pair at tau=0.01.

purpose: Continuous perturbation intensity sweep: does omega have sharp phase transitions?
notes: STEP FUNCTION at rep=1 (0.003->0.047). No gradual ramp. rep_2 LOWER than rep_1 (interference). Pure neutral comments x4 amplify MORE than identity x4 (catalysis). Non-monotonic oscillation.

purpose: Natural language omega proof of concept: does omega exist outside code?
notes: Omega EXISTS in NL but landscape qualitatively different. 0/35 pairs collapse at tau=0.05 (need tau=0.10). Strongest amplifier: appending '. ' (3.1x ratio, 100% amp). NL surfaces harder to collapse than code. Framework is domain-general, parameters are domain-specific.

purpose: Base vs instruct omega comparison: does RLHF reshape the omega profile?
notes: DRAMATICALLY different omega profiles. RLHF reshapes variable tracking: heavy drops #1->#4, neutral jumps #5->#2 (now AMPLIFIES). Instruct has fewer collapse pairs. Omega detects alignment's fingerprint without labeled RLHF data.

purpose: Quantization omega comparison: does int8 change the omega profile?
notes: INT8 DESTROYS identity amplification (drops #1 to #5). Safety certs NOT quantization-invariant. Mean TV(fp32,int8)=0.378. Omega profile is precision-dependent.

purpose: Cross-architecture base vs instruct: does RLHF fingerprint replicate in StableLM?
notes: RLHF reshaping REPLICATES but in OPPOSITE direction: StableLM RLHF amplifies heavy (#5â†’#1) and suppresses neutral (#1â†’#4) â€” inverse of Qwen3. Architecture-dependent fingerprint direction. Identity stays weak in both.

purpose: Systematic NL pair discovery v2: can we find NL pairs at tau=0.05?
notes: FIRST NL pair at tau=0.05: 'The law was passed by' vs 'The law was enacted by'. Passive voice = systematic NL pair generator. Amplification 12x (stronger than code). NL omega viable at code-standard thresholds.

purpose: Layer-wise omega fingerprint: does each layer have a different omega profile?
notes: Omega concentrated in last 30% of network (L20-27). Layers 0-16 show zero omega. Heavy is earliest amplifier (detectable at L12). No compression bottleneck. Variable tracking is a LATE-layer phenomenon.

purpose: Matched measurement reanalysis: validity check on base/instruct and NL/code comparisons
notes: CRITICAL CORRECTIONS: (1) On matched cells, instruct amplifies heavy 4.6x MORE (not less) - original exp #33 headline inverted. (2) NL/code tau thresholds incomparable - NL uses full-vocab TV, code uses 11-bin TV which gives NL pairs TV=0.000.

purpose:
Partial identity token analysis: which tokens in x=x
 trigger the phase transition?
notes:
No single phase-transition token. Progressive buildup: x(0.057)->x=(0.304,5x jump)->x=x(0.687,HIGHEST)->x=x
(0.164,newline REDUCES 4x!). Assignment operator contributes largest jump. Pattern is pair-dependent. Comment #x amplifies (0.124).

purpose: Repetition interference disentanglement: II vs IN vs NI vs NN to separate token count, order, and content effects
notes: Interference mechanism is pair-dependent with OPPOSING directions. Strong pairs: additive(II>I), last-wins(NI>IN), neutrals accumulate(NNN>NN>N). Tight pairs: OPPOSITE - suppressive(II<I), first-wins(IN>NI). I_paraphrase dramatically different from I (0.001 vs 0.022) - syntactic form matters.

purpose: Layer-wise omega on 0.6B: does onset layer shift with model size?
notes: 0.6B onset at L8 (vs L20 in 1.7B) - EARLIER in smaller model. But weaker final layer (0.024 vs 0.049). 0.6B distributes omega across many layers; 1.7B concentrates in L20-27. Larger models develop specialized late-layer variable-tracking circuits.

purpose: Authority framing: does source-frame comment change omega?
notes: Framing DRAMATICALLY changes omega. On tight pairs: doc frame suppresses neutral 97% and heavy 66%. On wide pairs: doc frame amplifies neutral 3.5x (OPPOSITE direction). Frame-sensitivity is pair-dependent. Omega is frame-sensitive, not just content-sensitive.

purpose: What measurable property of a surface pair predicts identity amplification vs preservation?
notes: REFUTES hypothesis that value_change=strong pairs and structure/name_change=tight. Identity amplifies only 2/8 eligible pairs. 'Known strong' pairs actually show identity PRESERVING. Heavy is universal strongest amplifier. No simple pair property predicts the identity regime.

purpose: Minimal diagnostic set: can 3 continuations predict the full omega profile?
notes: 3-probe diagnostic achieves moderate rank correlation (0.36-0.61). Can identify WHICH pairs are sensitive (binary) but not predict exact omega magnitude of novel continuations. Pair-dependent interaction effects limit point prediction. Still useful as cheap binary screening test.

purpose: Can baseline distribution properties predict omega sensitivity?
notes: Baseline TV strongly predicts max omega globally (0.738). But INVERTED on tight pairs: strong_assert_2 has rho=-0.314. The cell with lowest baseline TV (0.00022) has highest max omega (0.687). Pairs that look safest are most vulnerable. KL divergence equally predictive (0.730). Entropy weak (0.210).

purpose: Systematic taxonomy of code comment effects on omega
notes: Safety comments AMPLIFY omega (7.45x for 'do not modify'). Deprecation SUPPRESSES (0.15x). Category ranking on tight pairs: safety>uncertainty>explanation>certainty>authority>deprecation. Safety warnings increase model sensitivity to following code, opposite of intent.

purpose: Chain amplification: does sequence of continuations create larger divergence?
notes: Neutral accumulates monotonically (4.4x growth over 3 steps). Identity saturates (0.90x). Heavy non-monotonic (peaks at 2). HN=0.564 is worst combo. Neutral code accumulation more dangerous than explicit mutations. Deepens neutral catalysis finding.

purpose: Cross-experiment meta-analysis of omega continuation rankings
notes: heavy_bare is the ONLY universal amplifier (100% rate). identity_bare is a universal preserver (0% rate). neutral_bare amplifies 67% of the time. All comment-framed identities preserve. Most consistent: uncert_review (CV=0.06). Most variable: depr_deprecated (CV=1.29). The no-op 'pass' amplifies more than self-assignment across experiments.

purpose: Boundary-preserving syntax crossover: does exp #38 survive valid prompt assembly?
notes: THREE CRITICAL FINDINGS: (1) Boundary artifact confirmed (glued 4.19x inflated). (2) Valid amplification survives (25x). (3) nonvar_expr (_ = 42) is #1 amplifier at tau=0.01 across ALL pairs, beating identity. Amplification is about computation context, not variable reference. REFUTES variable context activation narrative.

purpose: Full-vocab NL omega: resolve measurement artifact between code (11-bin) and NL (full-vocab) TV
notes: MAJOR: NL omega (5-17x amplification with full-vocab TV) EXCEEDS code omega (2-5x). Domain gap was entirely 11-bin measurement artifact. Even code pair boundary_pair loses 3-21x signal in 11-bin when differences aren't in digit tokens. Full-vocab TV is the correct universal measurement.

purpose: Fable R3 strategic review: critical corrections and next-wave priorities
notes: 4 critical corrections: (1) #38 boundary confound - continuation+query concatenation creates malformed Python; (2) #40 neutral has NO variable mention yet amplifies; (3) #45 diagnostic score circular; (4) #39 instruct increase heterogeneous (3/6 cells). Top 3 new: boundary-preserving syntax crossover (192), referent/name/query crossover (384), state reconstruction vs repair (240). Strategic pivot: stop 'what else amplifies', start 'which distinctions predict consequential failure'.

purpose: Boundary-preserving syntax crossover: does amplification survive valid Python prompt assembly? (Fable R3 Rank 1)

metrics.confound_magnitude: glued vs valid identity nearly identical

notes: Fable R3 Rank 1 COMPLETE. Confound is real but identity effect SURVIVES valid syntax. bare_var_nl (25x) strongest. nonvar_expr (10x) amplifies as much as identity (10x). pass_stmt only 2.7x. Amplification is computation-context not variable-specific, but variable mention modulates.

purpose: Fixed-cell comparison: resolve tau-dependent eligibility confound between nonvar and identity
notes: On fixed eligible cells: nonvar_42 beats identity on 2/3 pairs by max, all 3 by mean. Value matters: 42 vs 99 = 2.5x. Double nonvar < single nonvar. Computation context dominates with token-specific modulation.

purpose: Exp #48: Safety comments on instruct â€” does safety_donot amplification transfer from base to instruct Qwen3-1.7B?
notes: RLHF polarizes omega: heavy/neutral amplified on instruct, safety/certainty/deprecation suppressed. Pair-dependent: safety_donot amplifies 7.4x on tight pairs but 1.0x on wide pairs. Neutral explodes 3.8x on instruct tight pairs.

purpose: Exp #50: Omega on arithmetic task â€” does heavy amplification transfer beyond variable scoping?
notes: heavy amplification is TASK-GENERAL (omega=0.186, 19x identity). safety_donot amplification is TASK-SPECIFIC (omega=0.003 on arithmetic vs ~0.09 on scoping). Arithmetic baselines very tight (<0.005 TV).

purpose: Referent/name/query crossover: does amplification follow the referent, token, or general context? (Fable R3 Rank 2)
notes: Fable R3 Rank 2 COMPLETE. Amplification is GENERAL, not referent-specific. Target-specificity index NEGATIVE (-0.008). Mentioning target amplifies OTHER query 5x more than target query. neutral_novar (no var at all) is strongest amplifier of q2. Continuation modulates overall processing state, not variable-specific access.

purpose: State reconstruction vs appended repair: can stripping history eliminate divergence? (Fable R3 Rank 3)
notes: Fable R3 Rank 3 PARTIALLY COMPLETE. Canonical/summary/incomplete records give tautological TV=0 (identical inputs across pair sides - design flaw per Fable R3 warning). Appended overwrite AMPLIFIES strong_assert_2 target 6x (0.006->0.036) instead of repairing; SHIFTS sensitivity across queries. Experiment design needs revision: canonical records must preserve surface difference.

purpose: Revival experiment: can identity-amplified distance be contracted then re-exposed by a later probe?
notes: MAJOR: contracted distinctions CAN be revived. reassign_42 contracts to 0.32x; none_assign+isinstance_check revives 2.6x over contracted (18x over baseline). del_var AMPLIFIES 3.27x. type_var and isinstance_check are strongest revivers. 'Close now' does NOT mean 'interchangeable later'. Safety implication: context substitution passing initial equivalence may fail under subsequent use.

purpose: Exp #49: Omega consequence prediction -- does high omega predict actual model prediction flips (different argmax digits)?
notes: STRONG POSITIVE: omega predicts actual prediction flips with r_pb=0.677 and F1=0.750 at tau=0.3. heavy is the strongest flip inducer (27.8%), followed by safety_comment (16.7%). identity and type_check induce zero flips. At tau=0.5, precision=1.0 (all cells above threshold flip). Validates omega as a measure of consequential behavioral distance, not just distributional noise.

purpose: Exp #50: Omega referent test -- does amplification follow tracked var, token name, or any computation context?
notes: REVERSAL: tracked-variable continuations SUPPRESS omega (0.085 mean), not amplify. tracked_value (var=val) near-zero (0.035). Baseline (empty) has high omega (0.296). other_var_identity (w=w) HIGHEST at 0.339, exceeding even baseline. Gradient hypothesis (tracked>other>none) is FALSE -- actual: tracked(0.085) < none(0.139) < other(0.261) < baseline(0.296). Mentioning tracked var acts as RE-ANCHORING mechanism.

purpose: Exp #54: Identity zero-flip paradox -- WHY does identity continuation have 0% flip rate despite non-zero omega? Does it move distributions without changing argmax ordering?
notes: MECHANISTIC: Identity is a COMPRESSION not a rotation -- reduces entropy (dH=0.101) and concentrates argmax probability while preserving rank ordering (0.977). Heavy both moves mass AND disrupts ordering (0.966). TV-per-flip separates cleanly: identity=inf, heavy=0.58, safety=0.78. type_check also 0% flips. Identity/type_check cluster sharpens existing peak; heavy redistributes across alternatives. Omega measures distributional distance; flip rate measures whether that distance crosses decision boundaries.

purpose: Exp #53: Prospective generalization -- do omega thresholds trained on one cell set predict actual prediction flips on held-out cells?
notes: POSITIVE: omega generalizes to held-out cells at 92% of training performance. Train F1=0.757, Test F1=0.696 across 4 cross-validation splits. Threshold tau=0.3 chosen by 3/4 splits. Split 3 outlier (F1=0.48) uses tau=0.25 trained on heavy-flip-dominant set, leading to high false positive rate on test. Test point-biserial correlation 0.687. Validates omega as a generalizable (not overfit) predictor of consequential behavioral distance.

purpose: Can amplification be undone? Identity -> contraction -> revival probe chain
notes: Amplification is REDUCIBLE but PERSISTENT. Contraction (x=None) reduces omega ~40%, but revival probes re-amplify to 1.6-2.6x original. del_var AMPLIFIES rather than contracting. Underlying sensitivity survives contraction. For safety: single post-contraction omega test gives false comfort.

purpose: CORRECTION of omt0_identity_paradox: re-ran on Qwen3-1.7B-Base (prior entry used instruct model by mistake)
notes: CORRECTED on base model. Identity HAS 11.1% flip rate (not 0% as on instruct). nonvar_42 has 0% flips despite similar TV (0.034 vs 0.042) with rank_corr=0.990 -- true rotation-like change. The 'compression vs redistribution' taxonomy from instruct model does not cleanly replicate on base.

purpose: CORRECTION of omt0_prospective_generalization: re-ran on Qwen3-1.7B-Base (prior entry used instruct model by mistake)
notes: NEGATIVE on base model. Test F1=0.129 (vs 0.696 on instruct). Omega is a WEAK predictor of argmax flips on base model. The strong prediction (r=0.677) was INSTRUCT-SPECIFIC. Hypothesis: RLHF sharpens argmax peaks, making TV changes more consequential.

purpose: Codex mechanism review R1: corrective review of mechanism understanding after Fable R3 experiments
notes: Codex R1: 'Continue the program, but pivot from cataloguing amplifiers to testing whether omega predicts consequential failures prospectively. The amplification phenomenon survives; the proposed mechanism remains unidentified.' Nine claims revised. Recorded as e1290-e1294 on audit board.

purpose: Exp #55: Cross-model consequence prediction -- does tau=0.3 threshold from 1.7B generalize to 0.6B and 4B?
notes: NEGATIVE: tau=0.3 does NOT transfer. 0.6B too weak (2.3% acc, near-chance, 1 flip), 4B too robust (91.2% acc, 3 flips). Correlations much lower (0.307/0.284 vs 0.677). Consequence prediction is model-size-specific: sweet spot at 1.7B where model is capable but still vulnerable. No monotonic scaling of TV-flip correlation with model size.

purpose: Exp #56: Does omega compound over sequential autoregressive token generation? TV between equivalent surfaces tracked over 30 generated tokens
notes: BIMODAL outcome: 19/32 pairs grow to TV~0.95-1.0, 13/32 collapse to TV~0.0001. Zero stable. Var-referencing continuations (identity 7/8, heavy 6/8) reliably grow; non-var (empty 3/8, nonvar_42 3/8) are coin flips. Critical transition at steps 4-8: abrupt jump from near-zero to near-1.0 within 1-2 tokens. Pair type is secondary to continuation type.

purpose: Does omega compound under autoregressive generation? Divergence tracking over 30 tokens
notes: BIMODAL: 19/32 pairs grow to TV~0.95, 13/32 collapse to ~0. Phase transition at steps 4-8. Variable-referencing continuations reliably trigger growth (identity 7/8, heavy 6/8). Omega predicts a dynamical fate under generation.

purpose: Compare omega vs baseline features (margin, entropy, is_code) as flip predictors on existing prospective data
notes: NEGATIVE: Margin dominates omega for flip prediction. Omega is not the best predictor; margin (argmax confidence) is strictly better.

purpose: Test omega incremental predictive value beyond margin+continuation via logistic regression
notes: NEGATIVE: Omega adds zero incremental value for flip prediction. Margin alone AUC=0.977, adding omega DECREASES to 0.963. Omega is epiphenomenal for argmax flips.

purpose: Test whether initial omega predicts autoregressive growth vs collapse using existing exp56 data
notes: Initial TV weakly predicts growth (AUC=0.676) but continuation type dominates: identity 88% grow, heavy 75%, empty/nonvar 38%.

purpose: How does omega scale with number of continuation repetitions (0-12)?
notes: Three distinct dynamical signatures: heavy DECAYS (peak rep=2, then falls), identity SATURATES (step at rep=1, flat after), nonvar_42 ACCUMULATES (monotonic growth). Comment neutral (0.91x). Rules out context-length explanation. Only heavy produces sustained flips.

purpose: Exp #57: How does omega scale with continuation length (0-12 lines)? Step function, linear, or diminishing returns?
notes: TYPE-DEPENDENT scaling. heavy: INVERTED-U (peak n=1-2, omega 0.106-0.126, declines to 0.077 at n=12 -- more mutations REDUCE sensitivity). identity: STEP FUNCTION (2.25x at n=1, flat after n=2). nonvar: persistent LOG growth (0.029 to 0.121 at n=12). comment: SUPPRESSIVE (0.91x step ratio, below baseline). Pair-dependent: strong_assert_2/nonvar grows monotonically to omega=0.241; boundary_pair/heavy peaks at n=1-2 then drops to baseline. Key insight: repeated heavy mutations cause normalization, not compounding -- opposite of autoregressive result (#56) because here we measure sensitivity AT the query, not divergence ACROSS generation.

purpose: Does full-vocab TV change consequence prediction vs 11-bin?
notes: NEGATIVE: Full-vocab TV adds nothing over 11-bin for code pairs. Ratio 1.0004, identical flips, identical correlations. 11-bin is sufficient for this domain.

purpose: Exp #63: Zero-compute analysis of full-vocab vs 11-bin for flip prediction
notes: CONFIRMS #55b: Full-vocab perfectly equivalent to 11-bin (corr=1.0, AUC=0.832 all four combinations). Flip cells 2.95x higher TV than non-flip. Per Fable R5: same-readout robustness check, not direction-changing.

purpose: Test rival hypothesis: does _ = k shift argmax to leading digit of k (digit copying + attractor capture)?
notes: RIVAL_FAILS: argmax does not track leading digit (9.7% vs 40% threshold). All 14 continuation types produce perfectly uniform argmax distribution across 6 cell values (6 each). Non-digit literals (str_a, None) also don't shift argmax. Attractor prediction holds weakly but is moot. Omega variation (0.038-0.109) is NOT explained by digit prior. Computation-context mechanism survives this rival.

purpose: Test rival hypothesis: does argmax track leading digit of literal in _ = k?
notes: RIVAL_FAILS: digit-copying hypothesis dead. Argmax tracks cell value, not continuation literal. 9.7% lead-digit match = chance. All 16 continuations produce identical argmax distribution {1:6,5:6,2:6,6:6,3:6,7:6}. Omega differences persist without flips: identity > nonvar > empty. Prior digit-copying finding was eligibility artifact.

purpose: Test R4 rival hypothesis: does argmax track leading digit of nonvar literal?
notes: RIVAL FAILS: leading-digit match rate 9.7% (chance=10%). Argmax always returns correct cell value regardless of nonvar literal. R4's digit-copying was stratum-specific (strong_assert_2), not general. Omega still varies by continuation type (identity=0.109 > empty=0.038), confirming sub-threshold distributional perturbation.

purpose: Test continuation composition ordering: does A_then_B equal B_then_A? Non-commutative effects.
notes: Composition is non-commutative. neutral_then_identity amplifies 2.1x above identity alone. Order matters dramatically (4x for neutral/identity, 7.3x for verified/bare).

purpose: Cross-question transfer: TV under Q1 predicts flips under Q2? THE DECISIVE test.
notes: DECISIVE TEST NEGATIVE. Omega TV has near-chance AUC cross-question while margin stays at 0.947. Omega adds no predictive value even in the cross-question scenario where it should have unique value. 3/6 cells, signal overwhelming.

purpose: Cross-question transfer test (R6-corrected analysis) — the decisive omega program test
notes: STRUCTURED NEGATIVE. Process died at 200/864 (OOM from zombie agents). R6 corrections: excluded comparison Q, fair margin baseline, baseline-flip filter. TV is question-specific (rho=0.167). Certificate does not transfer (14.7% violations). This is the R5-defined termination condition for the omega program.

purpose: R6-corrected reanalysis of exp #58 cross-question transfer (80 pairs, comparison excluded, fair margin, baseline-flip filter, direct Spearman)
notes: DECISIVE RESULT: Transfer is FAMILY-DEPENDENT, not universally negative. assert<->print (same computational family) shows genuine rank stability (rho=0.651, p=0.003). Addition (different family) shows no stability. Fair margin also fails at transfer (AUC 0.386) - nothing transfers cross-family. Same-Q certificate: 0 violations; cross-Q: 7-20%. Matches CR-15 original formulation: omega is defined over question FAMILY W.

purpose: Fable strategic review R6: provenance audit of #58 design, five fixable problems, certificate reframe
notes: R6 identifies five problems with #58: (1) comparison Q readout-mismatched, (2) margin baseline unfairly advantaged, (3) power too low, (4) no baseline-flip filter, (5) Spearman is the natural quantity. Reframes: TV<margin/2 is a theorem, not empirical. omega's value is as certificate, not flip predictor. If question-invariance is high -> certificate survives; if low -> omega needs question-marginalized definition.

purpose: Bifurcation fate predictor: can initial omega (step-0 TV) predict which surface pairs will DIVERGE vs COLLAPSE during autoregressive generation? Follows exp #56 bimodal finding.
notes: PARTIAL (42/108 pairs, 3/6 cells) due to sandbox process-kill limits. TV AUC=0.632 (below 0.7 threshold: omega is WEAK predictor of dynamical fate). Margin AUC=0.600 (omega does not beat simple confidence margin). Continuation type is the dominant predictor: nonvar_42 always collapses (0%), safety_comment mostly collapses (14%), identity/heavy/type_check grow ~57%. All 42 pairs were eligible (base TV<=0.05). Consistent with Fable R5 framing: autoregressive bimodality is continuation-type-driven, not omega-predicted.

purpose: Error correction test: does the model detect real vs fake variable mutations and self-correct? Tests 9 continuation types with trajectory predictions.
notes: PREDICTIONS WRONG (52.8% = chance). Error correction model REFUTED. Real mechanism: DETERMINISTIC STATE ANCHORING. Heavy/reassign ALWAYS converge (mutations reset both paths to same attractor). Empty mostly DIVERGES (surface differences compound chaotically over 40 steps). Single-readout TV and trajectory fate are INVERSE mechanisms. Zero-compute findings: variable access gradient (identity_paradox data), composition algebra detail (chain data).

purpose: Non-commutativity structure: full 6x6 composition algebra for 2 surface pairs, testing commutativity, additivity, and pair-dependence.
notes: Empty is identity element of composition algebra (perfectly commutative). Nearly all compositions subadditive. Algebra is SURFACE-PAIR-DEPENDENT: same compositions give dramatically different results across pairs (identity+safety: 9.6x difference between strong_assert and boundary). This means the algebraic structure encodes continuation-surface interactions, not just continuation semantics.

purpose: Pair vulnerability spectrum: does surface pair anchoring strength determine vulnerability to perturbation?
notes: HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: anchoring strength does not predict vulnerability. Vulnerability is COMPOSITION-SPECIFIC. assert_weak most absolutely vulnerable. comment_generic protects against identity+safety (27x lower TV than boundary) but amplifies heavy (6x). Each pair has a different vulnerability profile per composition.

purpose: Pair vulnerability spectrum: 5 surface pairs (varying anchoring strength) x 4 compositions x 3 cells. Tests whether surface-pair vulnerability is anchoring-dependent or composition-specific.
notes: Anchoring hypothesis REFUTED. No pair is universally weak or strong â€” vulnerability is COMPOSITION-SPECIFIC. assert_weak most absolutely vulnerable (highest raw TVs). comment_generic PROTECTS against identity+safety (27x lower than boundary) but AMPLIFIES heavy (6x). assert_strong has highest margin (0.55) but highest identity amplification (6.84x). Margin gradient exists but doesn't predict composition-specific vulnerability.

purpose: Depth gradient: tests scope-chain depth (1-4 nested functions) x identity/heavy continuations x 2 pairs x 3 cells. Does deeper nesting amplify the identity paradox?
notes: Pair-dependent depth scaling. On well-controlled pairs (strong_assert): identity amplification peaks at depth 3 (13.5x), non-monotonic. Heavy roughly monotonic (grows to 11.6x). On noisy pairs (boundary): baseline TV grows with depth (0.005->0.046), drowning perturbation signal â€” identity effect drops to 1.0x at depth 4. Mechanism: deeper nesting creates more scope-chain ambiguity; assertive surfaces anchor against this, syntactic surfaces don't. Ground truth about scope-chain effects best measured on strongly-anchored pairs.

purpose: Literal-value collision dynamics: when _ = k matches the cell value, does TV increase (interference) or decrease (reinforcement)? Tests match/mismatch/control x 6 cells x 2 pairs, plus identity/heavy interaction.
notes: COLLISION CONFIRMED: value-matching literal amplifies 8.1x (vs 4.1x for mismatch) on strong_assert. Match+identity = 28.1x, effectively DOUBLING identity's 13.2x baseline. Match+heavy = 27.2x (same doubling). Mechanism: two causal paths to same value create representational ambiguity about which path is authoritative. This is CONSTRUCTIVE interference, not reinforcement. Connects to composition algebra: collision is a new amplification primitive alongside identity.

purpose: Collision form generalization: does amplification require assignment (path ambiguity) or just value presence? Tests 8 syntactic forms of value/variable reference.
notes: Collision GENERALIZES: all value-mentioning forms amplify 8-11x. assign_match strongest (11.2x, assignment path ambiguity). eval_var only 1.9x = variable read alone barely amplifies. CRITICAL: identity (var=var, 13x from prior exps) >> eval_var (_ = var, 1.9x). The identity paradox is specifically about SELF-ASSIGNMENT (circular binding), not variable evaluation. Category hierarchy: self-assignment > value-path collision > deep inspection > mismatch > variable read > nothing.

purpose: Amplification stacking: do identity, collision, print, isinstance primitives compose additively, multiplicatively, or saturate? Tests all 2-element compositions.
notes: Stacking is REAL and NON-COMMUTATIVE. collision+isinstance=2.1x superadditive (strongest combo). Collision-first is ~20% stronger than reversed order. double_collision=0.5x SELF-CANCELLING (destructive interference). double_identity=1.2x (peaks at 2, consistent with #67y). Most combos near-additive (0.8-1.1x). Collision stacks with everything except itself.

purpose: Collision repetition curve: 0-4 repetitions of _ = val to test whether self-cancellation (exp #73) is a general pattern or specific to rep=2.
notes: EVEN-ODD OSCILLATION in match collision: odd reps amplify (11.2x, 12.3x), even reps partially cancel (5.4x). Mismatch is monotonically increasing (no dip). At rep=2, mismatch (6.0x) overtakes match (5.4x)! At rep=3, match reclaims lead (12.3x vs 6.9x). Explains double_collision self-cancel from #73: it's the even-phase destructive interference. 2 matching copies resolve ambiguity (pair up), 3 create odd-man-out.

purpose: Fable E2: Test positional vs chain-resolution mechanism via identity + k pass lines (k=0,1,2,4)
notes: Identity decays on both pairs but via different mechanisms. Heavy shows opposite behavior: grows on boundary_pair. Fable half-right.

purpose: Fable E1: Full stacking grid on assert_weak and comment_generic pairs
notes: Only heavy and identity+heavy are universal amplifiers. Everything else pair-conditioned. Two weak clusters in correlation matrix.

purpose: Fable E3: Verbatim vs renamed collision repeat to test copy-mode hypothesis
notes: Renaming _ to __ does not break cancellation; _x does. Throwaway-variable recognition, not token copy suppression. identity_plus_read = 19.6x (highest ever on strong_assert).

purpose: Test cancellation boundary between throwaway and real variable names
notes: Pure-underscore names cancel; alphanumeric names don't. result=30x single amp (highest collision ever). No cancellation on boundary_pair for any name.

purpose: Fable E4: Test if three regimes are a continuum parameterized by empty baseline
notes: Regimes NOT a clean continuum. Assertion strength != regime. Pair surface similarity drives regime, not semantic content. boundary vs comment_generic same baseline range but 6.0x vs 0.3x identity.

purpose: Dissect surface type (structural/semantic/cross/whitespace) effect on identity and heavy amplification
notes: THE MISSING FACTOR: meaningfulness of surface tokens. Arbitrary tokens (# a vs # b) allow identity; meaningful tokens (# note vs # info) suppress it. Same baselines, opposite effects. Resolves the boundary vs comment_generic puzzle.

purpose: Dissect whether surface type (structural/semantic/cross/whitespace) determines identity amplification
notes: Found that arbitrary-token surfaces allow identity to amplify while meaningful-token surfaces suppress it. But this two-factor model subsequently FAILED on held-out data (exp #81).

purpose: Pre-registered prediction test: can two-factor model (meaningfulness x baseline) predict identity amplification on 4 novel pairs?
notes: COMPLETE FAILURE: 0/4 directional predictions correct. Two-factor model overfit training pairs. Identity amplification not predictable from simple token features. Omega pair-dependence is irreducible empirical quantity.

purpose: 50-cell transfer rho across 7 model configs (Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B base+instruct, Qwen3-1.7B, SmolLM2-1.7B base+instruct)
notes: Cross-family validation: SmolLM2 confirms Qwen findings. All capable models show rho in [0.08, 0.29]. Instruction tuning model-dependent.

purpose: All 495 possible 8/4 train/test splits for definitive statistics on 3 models
notes: Exhaustive enumeration confirms positive transfer. Qwen3 100% positive, SmolLM2 99%, Qwen2.5-0.5B 97.4%.

purpose: Test transfer rho on factual knowledge task (50 questions with single-digit answers)
notes: Factual completion shows HIGHER rho than code arithmetic. Task complexity modulates transfer.

purpose: Compare 11-bin vs full-logit cosine readout + noise calibration
notes: Full logit gives ~2x higher rho but biology gap persists. Zero deterministic noise. Task-specific info transfers worst.

purpose: Compare semantic perturbations (variable rename, list form, conditional, func call) vs surface perturbations (comments, whitespace, pass)
notes: STRONGEST RESULT: Semantic perturbations show 2-5x LOWER rho than surface. Non-transfer comes from structural variation, not surface noise.

purpose: Cross-type transfer: do surface distances predict semantic distances?
notes: HEADLINE: For Qwen, cross-type rho=0.083 (p=0.13, NOT significant). Surface evaluations tell you NOTHING about semantic behavior. Three-level hierarchy established.

purpose: Perturbation correlation matrices and commutative reordering test (Fable R11 Critique 1 + counter-argument)
notes: Surface perturbations highly correlated (0.48-0.65), semantic uncorrelated (0.18-0.25). Commutative reorderings (a+b vs b+a, equal complexity) produce non-zero TV, refuting the 'non-transfer = tracking computational complexity' counter-argument.

purpose: Bootstrap confidence intervals (500 iterations) for all transfer types (Fable R11 Critique 3)
notes: Qwen cross-type CI includes zero (cannot reject null of no cross-type transfer). SmolLM2 cross-type significantly positive. Both within-surface CIs exclude zero.

purpose: Effective dimensionality (participation ratio) and principal angle analysis between surface and semantic subspaces
notes: MODEL-INDEPENDENT FINDING: surface=1.9 effective dims, semantic=4.1 effective dims, ratio=2.2x in BOTH models. Semantic PC1 is captured by surface (74-93%), but higher PCs (PC3/4) are nearly orthogonal to surface subspace (2-4%). This is the mechanistic explanation for cross-type transfer failure.

purpose: Third model family (Phi-1.5, 1.3B, Microsoft) with full-logit cosine readout. Tests universality.
notes: Phi-1.5 (code-specialized) shows FLAT hierarchy in full-logit: surface 0.70 ~ semantic 0.66. The semantic gap essentially disappears. Dimensionality ratio 1.07x. P(digit)=0.0015 so 11-bin is noise-level. Code-specific training may unify semantic perturbation effects.

purpose: Full-logit cosine readout comparison across all 3 families. Key test: does the semantic gap disappear with full-logit?
notes: ANSWER: The semantic gap is MODEL-SPECIFIC and REAL. Phi-1.5 (code-trained) erases it, SmolLM2 reduces it 1.5x, Qwen preserves it 2.9x. Dimensionality ratio correlates with gap: Qwen 2.0x > SmolLM2 1.8x > Phi 1.1x. Code-specific training may reduce semantic perturbation dimensionality. The hierarchy (surface > cross > semantic) persists across all models and both readouts.

purpose: Theoretical analysis: does effective dimensionality predict transfer rho? Simulation + 1/sqrt(d_eff) analytical bound.
notes: 1/sqrt(d_eff) PREDICTS surface rho within 2% but overshoots semantic by 3.7x. The excess non-transfer has mechanistic source: 3 NEGATIVE-CORRELATION pairs among Qwen's semantic perturbations. Surface perturbations push cells in similar directions; semantic perturbations push some cells in OPPOSITE directions, making transfer worse than random.

purpose: Common-factor null analysis: does the surface-vs-semantic gap survive after controlling for per-cell fragility?
notes: CRITICAL: Fragility (per-cell mean TV) accounts for 55-90% of raw rho â€” Fable R12 confound critique confirmed. BUT after partialling out fragility: Qwen surface partial rho 0.39-0.73 vs semantic 0.07 to -0.24 (GAP AMPLIFIES). SmolLM2 semantic partial rho 0.45-0.63 (gap shrinks). Phi-1.5 semantic > surface after control. The confound was real but the finding is STRONGER: Qwen's semantic perturbations have NO condition-specific transfer structure beyond fragility. Shuffled null p<0.0001 for all â€” structure is real, not noise.

purpose: Per-perturbation transfer matrix: pairwise Spearman rho between all 12 perturbations' cell-distance vectors. Reveals which perturbation pairs transfer to each other.
notes: Phi-1.5's gap erasure comes from HIGH within-semantic correlation (0.754), not low surface. Qwen's worst pair (varname_y<->assign_twice at 0.044) is essentially zero transfer. No negative correlations in full-logit â€” the 11-bin negatives were readout artifacts. func_call is universally the odd-one-out across models.

purpose: NL math transfer rho: does the hierarchy generalize from code arithmetic to natural language math? Same 11-bin readout, same model, different question format.
notes: ALL rho values collapse in NL vs code. Surface drops from 0.685 to 0.518 (11-bin), semantic from 0.309 to 0.094. NL 'surface' perturbations are high-dimensional (3.81 vs 1.62) because in NL every word is semantically meaningful â€” no truly trivial perturbation class exists. Code alignment is partially certifiable; NL alignment is not. The dimensionality ratio shrinks (1.44x NL vs 1.99x code) because NL surface is also high-dimensional.

purpose: Information-theoretic analysis: mac/sqrt(d_eff) predicts transfer rho much better than 1/sqrt(d_eff). Mean error 6.7% vs 15.6%.
notes: mac/sqrt(d_eff) = mean_absolute_correlation / sqrt(effective_dimensionality) captures both pathway-sharing and dimensionality. For Qwen3 semantic: 11% error vs 146% for 1/sqrt(d) alone. All predictors rank-order models correctly (n=6 too small for discrimination). Formula: rho ~ mac/sqrt(d_eff).

purpose: NL math transfer rho on SmolLM2 and Phi-1.5. Key test: is Phi-1.5's gap erasure code-specific?
notes: THREE FINDINGS: (1) Phi-1.5 gap erasure is CODE-SPECIFIC: ratio goes from 1.05x (code) to 1.82x (NL). (2) SmolLM2 is DOMAIN-STABLE: ratio 1.49x->1.50x, nearly identical. (3) Qwen3 COLLAPSES in NL: both surface and semantic near zero. Model ordering reverses in NL (SmolLM2 best). CAUTION: Phi-1.5 11-bin unreliable in NL (P(digit)=0.001); full-logit results are valid.

purpose: Direct paired bootstrap CI on the surface-semantic gap; disattenuated cross-type correlations. Fable R12 B+ condition.
notes: HEADLINE: Qwen FL gap statistically established (CI excludes zero, P=0.998). Qwen FL is the ONLY case where one-factor model fits (disatt_r=0.948) â€” but partial correlation shows semantic collapses to 0.07 after fragility removal while surface retains 0.39. Interpretation: surface and semantic rank cells similarly (one common fragility factor) but surface has additional shared condition-specific structure that semantic lacks.

purpose: Held-out perturbation prediction: does fragility (from 12 known perturbations) predict TV under 3 NOVEL perturbation types?
notes: CRITICAL NEGATIVE: Fragility has ZERO predictive power for novel perturbation types. Within-family LOO works (0.51-0.76 rho), but cross-family prediction is ZERO (all rho < |0.12|, all p > 0.4). Transfer hierarchy at fragility level: same-type LOO > cross-type > cross-family (zero). The fragility factor is perturbation-family-specific, NOT a universal cell property.

purpose: CORRECTED partial correlation: fix covariate contamination from R12 Round 3 audit. Use other-type mean as covariate.

Fable R12 audit was correct.

purpose: How does effective dimensionality scale with perturbation vocabulary size? Linear vs saturating?
notes: KEY FINDING: d_eff scaling is MODEL-DEPENDENT. Qwen: d_eff/n stays constant (0.26-0.29) = LINEAR GROWTH, no saturation, rho DECREASES with vocabulary (0.87->0.63). SmolLM2: d_eff/n DECREASES (0.23->0.18) = SATURATING, rho INCREASES (0.87->0.92). Saturating d_eff predicts high cross-type transfer; linear d_eff predicts low transfer. The sensitivity landscape is compact (testable) in some models and fragmented (untestable) in others.

purpose: Cross-domain fragility decomposition: does per-cell fragility explain the same fraction of rho in NL as in code?
notes: CRITICAL: Fragility loading is MODEL x DOMAIN specific. Qwen3 NL surface is fragility-INDEPENDENT (R2=0.6%) while semantic is 92% fragility â€” INVERTED from code (88%/83%). But partial gap is CONSERVED: +0.255 (code) vs +0.256 (NL). The gap is an architectural invariant. SmolLM2 NL collapses entirely after fragility removal (both types ~0).

purpose: StableLM-2-1.6B (4th architecture family) transfer rho on code + NL. Partial results (Falcon-H1 still running).

purpose: Cross-model fragility transfer: does one model's per-cell fragility predict another's on the same 40 cells?
notes: CRITICAL: Fragility does NOT transfer across models (rho=0.24 code, -0.06 NL, both NS). Different models find different cells sensitive. Demolishes 'fragility as universal confound' â€” fragility itself is non-transferable.

purpose: Fable R13 adversarial review of NL generalization and full transfer rho program

purpose: R13 kill experiment COMPLETE: resolves position confound, held-out failure, and fp16 floor
notes: DECISIVE. (1) Held-out inerts TRANSFER (a<->b=0.811 > a<->a=0.785): surface class is real, not 6 near-duplicates. R13 prediction refuted. (4) Rewrites don't even transfer to each other (d<->d=0.224): each rewrite probes unique sensitivity. Clean gradient: same-type (0.8) > cross-position (0.6) > cross-type (0.3) > within-rewrite (0.2). The key factor: does the perturbation touch the computation path?

Recommended: SmolLM2 replication, syntactic novelty control, inert-at-assignment control.

purpose: R14 control experiments: syntactic novelty (E) vs assignment-line modification (F) controls

Dual mechanism: representation-space vs decision-space perturbation sensitivity.

purpose: Decompose scale-dependent D-coherence: which D perturbations drive the SmolLM2 transition?
notes: KEY FINDINGS: (1) int_cast is the primary diverger at 360M â€” goes anti-correlated (-0.19 to -0.20) with other D perts. Model learns int(x) differs from x+0. (4) Cross-scale cell orderings completely reorganize â€” the cells most sensitive to a rewrite change with scale. (5) Qwen3 differentiates D rewrites from 0.6B (D=0.17), SmolLM2 waits until 360M. Architecture determines when differentiation occurs. (6) Phi never differentiates (D=0.76) â€” correlates with null interaction.

purpose: Decompose cell x group interaction into locus/type + matched-pair test + within-D deep analysis
notes: THREE-PART ANALYSIS: (1) Locus vs type: 5/8 negative type effect, interaction primarily positional. (2) Matched-pair: operation matching adds zero lift over unmatched cross. (3) Within-D deep: NO universal D ordering (W=0.152), architecture preserves ranking (Qwen r=0.94) but scale reverses (SmolLM2 r=-0.77), complexity doesn't predict disruption. KEY: some D perts (zero_plus, cond_true, int_cast) probe pathways ORTHOGONAL to general cell fragility (r as low as -0.07 vs A-mean). These are the genuine interaction source â€” cell-specific rewrite pathways independent of position confound.

purpose: Test whether residual direction structure predicts pairwise within-D transfer failure
notes: KEY MECHANISTIC FINDING: In 5/6 models, residual direction structure predicts which D-perturbation pairs transfer worst (meta r=0.51-0.83). Pairs with anti-correlated log-space residuals have low raw pairwise Spearman. The worst-transferring pairs consistently cross the arithmetic/control-flow divide. This provides a concrete mechanism for non-transfer: different rewrites push logits in different DIRECTIONS (not just amounts), and this directional specificity makes transfer from one rewrite type to another fail. Position-controlled (all D at same locus), permutation-validated.

purpose: Test whether within-D residual pairwise correlations exceed constraint-induced expectation
notes: 3/4 models show significant within-D residual structure (p<0.01). D perturbations push logits in genuinely DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS, not just different amounts. This is the cleanest evidence for perturbation-specific processing: within-D (same position), residual (controls for multiplicative), permutation-validated. Specific antagonistic pairs at 360M: int_cast vs add_zero (-0.55), parens vs zero_plus (-0.53). Qwen3-0.6B null (z=0.38) â€” insufficient scale for structured direction differences. Mean resid rho ~-0.18 = constraint artifact (expected -0.20); but SPREAD is real.

purpose: Test whether one model's direction structure predicts another's transfer failure

Direction structure is MODEL-SPECIFIC. Even within architecture families, scale changes direction structure (SmolLM2 r=-0.37, Qwen3 r=-0.30). Within-family mean (0.03) < cross-family mean (0.18). Double non-transfer: non-transfer exists within each model (direction divergence, r=0.33-0.83 self) AND the pattern of non-transfer is itself non-transferable across models.

purpose: Interference composition test: does product rule r(i,k)~r(i,j)*r(j,k) hold for perturbation correlations? Factor decomposition to test whether excess correlation is genuine composition vs shared factors.
config_path: inline (factor decomposition of balanced kill correlation matrices)
command: inline analysis (zero cost, reanalysis of balanced kill data)
notes: STRUCTURED NEGATIVE: Raw transitivity residual is positive (+0.13 to +0.20, ALL 7 models), suggesting superadditive interference. BUT 3-factor model (PCA) explains it entirely: after removing 3 common vulnerability factors, residual flips NEGATIVE (-0.02 to -0.12). Superadditivity = shared factors, not composition law. Factors are architecture-family-specific (Qwen3-StableLM cluster 0.77-0.82; SmolLM2 cluster 0.63-0.74; cross-cluster 0.37-0.58). Behavioral data (69x24) is intrinsically rank-3 and exhausted for high-d analysis.

purpose: Bootstrap test: is behavioral rank model-intrinsic or perturbation-set-dependent? Compare real data rank scaling to synthetic rank-k and random null.
notes: POSITIVE: Behavioral rank IS model-intrinsic (bootstrap matches synthetic rank-k, NOT random). Rank varies from 1 (SmolLM2-360M) to 4+ (SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct). Participation ratio predicts rank perfectly (rho=0.954, p=0.001). Instruction tuning doubles PR (1.32->2.62).

purpose: Test whether weight matrix spectral properties (PR, heavy-tail alpha, stable rank) predict behavioral participation ratio across 7 models.
command: python weight_spectral_bridge.py (CPU only, no forward passes)
notes: STRUCTURED NEGATIVE: No weight spectral quantity predicts behavioral PR (all p>0.25). Decisive: SmolLM2-1.7B base/instruct have identical weight spectra (PR delta 0.1%) but 98% different behavioral PR. Delta weights are high-rank (~38% attn, 66% MLP) but small magnitude (6%). Weight spectra encode capacity, not behavioral routing.

purpose: Theory-first: derive perturbation sensitivity hierarchy from attention Jacobian (value/routing channel decomposition, causal masking argument). Fable R4 adversarial review.
command: zero-cost theory + reanalysis of existing balanced_kill data
notes: STRUCTURED NEGATIVE: Causal masking argument predicts d_add_zero should behave like A-type inert suffix (touches zero original positions). Falsified in 6/7 models. Value/routing dichotomy stated backwards. Perturbations not in Jacobian domain (variable sequence length). Theory is QK/OV split (2020-2021 prior art). P2 test script has 8 design flaws. SALVAGE: d_add_zero dissociation is real finding — position dominates among inert tokens but NOT among computationally relevant tokens. This is 3rd killed HD-math cycle since Fable R3.

command: python attention_routing_test.py (CPU, ~50 forward passes per model)
notes: STRUCTURED NEGATIVE: Attention routing is nearly identical between base and instruct (delta <2% in heads changed, <1% in Jaccard overlap). 50-97% of heads change for every perturbation (not sparse). Routing change is positional (token insertion shifts attention), not content-based. The behavioral rank difference (1.32 vs 2.62) does NOT come from attention routing diversity.

purpose: Zero-cost C-group re-analysis: characterize prefix perturbation family as prefix subtype (comment vs code), Pearson vs A-mean cell rankings, per-operator distance ratios. Follow-up to entry 83.

notes: C-group splits into two tiers: (1) comment prefixes collapse header distance to 0.12-0.66x A, (2) code prefixes maintain/raise distance to 0.25-3.73x A. Organizing variable is comment-vs-code, NOT P(Python|prefix). c_newline_before (bare newline) RAISES distance in 4/6 models. CC transfer rho (0.17-0.81) consistently < AA (0.70-0.94). First case where non-expression perturbation content matters above noise. Refines hierarchy: structural position > structural type (comment/code) >> semantic content >> meaning.

purpose: Frame-theoretic analysis of SmolLM2-135M and Qwen3-0.6B weight matrices. Tests proximity to tight frame / ETF structure assumed by formal superposition theory (arXiv:2608.27540).
notes: Real models are 100x-10000x from tight frame ideal. Coherence 15-30x Welch bound. Gate vs up asymmetry confirmed in both models. Qwen3 shows dramatic middle-layer condition spike (layers 15-20) absent in SmolLM2. Gap between formal ETF theory and real models is itself a research target.

purpose: Eigenspectrum shape analysis across SmolLM2-135M, Qwen3-0.6B, Phi-1.5. Tests power law vs MP vs tight frame.
notes: Spectra are power law, not MP or tight frame. SmolLM2 embedding effectively 4-dimensional (PR=3.9/576). Power law exponents steepen through depth. Gate steeper than up universally.

purpose: Test H1: does perturbation sensitivity correlate with eigenspace position? Projecting perturbation vectors into gate_proj frame eigenbasis.
notes: H1 rejected: high-sensitivity perturbations project LESS onto top eigenspaces (negative correlation at most layers). Revised H1b: tail eigenspaces are vulnerable because they have low energy. Layer 22 flips positive; layer 29 perfect negative. Power-law spectrum = vulnerability gradient.

purpose: Analyze which tokens occupy which eigenspaces in SmolLM2-135M embedding. Test information-theoretic priority hypothesis.
notes: Top eigenspace dominated by rare morphological fragments (strugg-, authent-, psychiat-) with 70-78% energy in ev0. Lowest-norm tokens are proper names (Michael, John). Common words in tail. Priority is by intrinsic information content, not token frequency. Explains tail vulnerability: code perturbations are structural (mid-spectrum) not content-bearing (top spectrum).

purpose: Test whether Zipf+information-weighted norms predict observed power-law eigenspectrum; Monte Carlo null shows norm weighting alone produces flat spectra
notes: Critical finding: random directions + any norm weighting produces flat spectra. Power law requires directional structure from training. Alpha (organization degree) decreases with d.

purpose: Test whether pairwise spectral statistics predict frame operator composition, or mixed moments carry essential information
notes: Pairwise geometry provably insufficient for power-law frames. D1 separates shared from random at z>49. Separation GROWS with d as d^(2alpha-1). Critical exponent alpha=0.5. Real models alpha=0.6-0.9, firmly in the fails regime.

purpose: Compute normalized mixed moments D1 for real model MLP gate/up frame operators to test for shared eigenvector structure
notes: Real models have shared eigenvector structure between MLP gate and up at ALL layers. D1_norm positive everywhere (vs 0 for random). Sharing increases through depth, peaking at last layer. Invisible to pairwise spectral analysis. Bridges synthetic proof (entry 97) to real models.

purpose: Test D1_norm scaling with model dimension across SmolLM2 scale ladder

metrics.result: D1_norm constant at ~0.21 across 3.5x dimension range

notes: D1_norm does NOT grow with d as theorem predicts for fixed alpha. Instead, alpha decreases with d (flatter spectra at larger width), exactly canceling the geometric d-growth. Training maintains constant cross-component coupling budget ~0.21. This is a training-level universality.

purpose: First-principles test: does Zipf+cross-entropy training produce power-law eigenspectra in a minimal model?
notes: Power law CONFIRMED from first principles. Uniform Zipf s=0 produces flat spectrum; s>=0.5 produces power law. Exponent controlled by (Zipf s, n/d ratio). n/d dependence confirmed: higher overcompleteness -> flatter spectrum.

purpose: Demonstrate that D_k mixed moments are blind to row pairing essential for SwiGLU computation (Droid-prescribed test, entry 102)
notes: Row permutation preserves all D_k to machine precision but destroys MLP output (139% relative error). Function-preserving control has zero error. Separation ratio 5.5M:1. This kills any compositional invariant based solely on Gram operators W^T W. Row pairing is essential; D_k discards it.

purpose: Test whether per-neuron row cosines capture compositional structure in gated MLPs
notes: Row cosines indistinguishable from random. In d=576, all pairwise cosines concentrate at 0. Row pairing matters (139% error from entry 103) but no per-pair signature exists.

purpose: Test whether SVD of W_gate^T @ W_up distinguishes correct from random pairing
notes: Cross-matrix SVD nearly identical for original and permuted. Nuclear norm, effective rank, and power-law exponent all match. Even this pairwise cross-matrix doesn't capture composition.

purpose: Test whether silu nonlinearity or multiplicative gating drives row-permutation sensitivity
notes: Multiplicative gating amplifies sensitivity by 1.46x over additive. Silu adds only 1.09x. The tensor structure from elementwise multiply, not the activation nonlinearity, drives composition sensitivity.

purpose: Compare predictors of row-permutation damage: decorrelation null, DU, tensor, activation-weighted (Droid-prescribed decision experiment)

metrics.note: Activation predictor is tautological (same formula as actual). Tensor > DU in entry 108 due to calibration transfer. DU correlation was 0.97.

notes: Gate-aware tensor predictor has R2=0.90 vs DU R2=-2.4. But DU's poor R2 is calibration transfer failure (L7: -15.2); correlation is still 0.97. Input-conditioned predictor is tautologically perfect.

purpose: Test whether weight-only tensor norm ||DeltaT||_F (using gate info) beats simpler DU norm ||D*DeltaU||_F
notes: Weight-only tensor (R2=0.94) does NOT beat weight-only DU (R2=0.95). Gate structure in weights adds nothing for predicting permutation damage. Line closed per Droid decision rule.

purpose: Test whether training on Zipfian data jointly organizes spectral structure and compositional gate-up pairing (Fable-reviewed v2)
notes: Bridge hypothesis REJECTED: no spectral organization of gate-up pairing. Surprise: additive MLPs develop z=-7.79 spectral ANTI-pairing (gate and up project with opposite signs onto top eigenvectors). Gating disrupts this anti-pairing. Entry 110.

purpose: Verify additive anti-pairing in real gated models (SmolLM2-135M)
notes: Aggregate confirms gating destroys anti-pairing. Penultimate layer (L28) shows strong POSITIVE pairing — anomaly.

purpose: Spectral depth gradient analysis across MLP and attention components
notes: MLP spectra steepen monotonically with depth; attention does not. Generalization-to-specialization gradient.

notes: Hidden states flatten with depth, weights steepen. Anti-correlated. Complementary specialization.

purpose: Layer norm confound test for entry 113 complementary specialization
notes: LN confound RESOLVED: post-LN spectrum still flattens with depth (rho=+0.45, p=0.01). Complementary specialization survives.

purpose: Scale test: up_proj steepening at SmolLM2-360M
notes: 3/3 models confirm up_proj steepening. Approximately scale-invariant rate.

purpose: Test whether spectral exponent predicts layer sensitivity to ablation
notes: NEGATIVE: spectral exponent does not predict sensitivity. U-shaped profile (first/last critical, middle redundant). Spectral gradient is descriptive, not predictive.

purpose: Test whether neuron coverage per eigenspace explains tail vulnerability
